results.title: Adversarial Attacks and Defenses in Explainable AI
results.content: This survey provides a comprehensive overview of research concerning adversarial attacks on explanations of machine learning models, as well as fairness metrics. *ACM Computing Surveys*, 2023  The rising popularity of explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) to understand high-performing black boxes raised the question of how to evaluate explanations of machine learning (ML) models. In this paper, we set out to systematize attacks against post-hoc explanation methods to lay the groundwork for developing more robust explainable machine learning. OpenXAI comprises of the following key components: (i) a flexible synthetic data generator and a collection of diverse real-world datasets, pre-trained models, and state-of-the-art feature attribution methods, (ii) open-source implementations of twenty-two quantitative metrics for evaluating faithfulness, stability (robustness), and fairness of explanation methods, and (iii) the first ever public XAI leaderboards to readily compare several explanation methods across a wide variety of metrics, models, and datasets. security   model   evaluation   deep   adversarial   defense   attacks   interpretability   robustness   adversarial-machine-learning   adversarial-examples   counterfactual   adversarial-attacks   explainable-ai   xai   interpretable   interpretable-machine-learning   iml   explainability   responsible-ai

results.content: # Applications of interpretable deep learning in neuroimaging: A comprehensive review *Open Access* Robinson, Maria Deprez, Po-Wah So; Applications of interpretable deep learning in neuroimaging: A comprehensive review. Therefore, deep learning (DL) has become a popular tool in neuroimaging in recent years, driven by the rise in computer processing power as well as increased access to large medical imaging datasets and the success of novel model architectures. Interpretable deep learning (iDL) has been proposed to address the opacity problem of DL models, for example, by producing explanations that highlight brain regions that are most relevant for the model predictions. results.title: TRiSM for Agentic AI: A Review of Trust, Risk, and Security ...
results.content: # TRiSM for Agentic AI: A Review of Trust, Risk, and Security Management in LLM-based Agentic Multi-Agent Systems This review presents a structured analysis of Trust, Risk, and Security Management (TRiSM) in the context of LLM-based Agentic Multi-Agent Systems (AMAS). We then adapt and extend the AI TRiSM framework for Agentic AI, structured around four key pillars: Governance, Explainability, ModelOps, and Privacy/Security , each contextualized to the challenges of multi-agent LLM systems.
